item_argument_dependencies.argument: Define the finite real Hermitian operator space, trace pairing, Gram matrix, Moore–Penrose inverse, and canonical dual; local well-definedness is proved by lem-nrqmx-finite-hermitian-trace-inner-product.
Prove reality, symmetry, positive definiteness, the induced norm, Gram positivity, synthesis-adjoint identity, and ker(G)=ker(S).
Identify the Gram Moore–Penrose inverse with its finite spectral formula and prove S G+ S*=I on a spanning Hermitian frame, including redundant-frame kernels.
Apply the choice-free bounded-variable MGF estimate to Bernoulli indicators, factor the finite product expectation, optimize Markov’s bound, and combine tails.
Represent each finite CP outcome map by Kraus operators, use trace preservation of their sum for isometry normalization, and project/trace the outcome register.
Prove the commuting construction and the converse support argument 0≤Gij≤Pi,Qj using finite positive square roots; recover the unique products.
Specify exact finite Gram, pseudoinverse, canonical dual, and frequency reconstruction steps; positivity is deliberately not imposed.
Use frame duality for exact recovery, the induced operator norm for deterministic error, Bernoulli indicator concentration and a finite union bound for the IID frequency statement.
Construct two normalized Kraus instruments with identical Z effects, verify both dilate under the A-page theorem, and compare their exact updates on |0><0|.

Compute the six-outcome Pauli POVM and Gram eigenspaces; use the local frame spectral pseudoinverse and canonical-dual definition to calculate exact reconstruction, then exhibit a simplex frequency vector whose output has a negative eigenvalue.

sources.title: John Watrous, The Theory of Quantum Information, author-hosted Chapter 2 PDF
sources.locator: Chapter 2 §§2.2.2 and 2.3.3, Theorem 2.22 and equations (2.255)–(2.262); printed pp. 79–83 and 111–113 (PDF pp. 21–24 and 53–55).
sources.reading_extent: The complete relevant Choi–Kraus, instrument, outcome-probability, and outcome-register passages were inspected in the 66-page Chapter 2 PDF; no claim is made that every chapter section was read for this batch.

contents.name: The finite Choi–Kraus representation and trace-preserving normalization, Theorem 2.22

source_review.read_extent: Read §2.2.2, including the statement and proof of Theorem 2.22.
source_review.supports: The finite CP-map Kraus representation and the criterion that a Kraus family is trace-preserving exactly when its adjoint products sum to identity.
source_review.limitations: The local supplier fixes the input-reference tensor output Choi convention; the new dilation proof uses only its Kraus and trace-preserving conclusions.

contents.name: General finite outcome instruments, equations (2.258)–(2.262)

source_review.read_extent: Read the definition and outcome probability/state-update discussion in §2.3.3, including the classical outcome-register construction.
source_review.supports: A finite outcome instrument is a family of completely positive maps whose sum is a channel, and it can be represented by attaching a classical outcome register.
source_review.limitations: The new item gives its own finite matrix construction and verifies the outcome projection and partial trace formula directly.

contents.name: POVM effects and state probabilities in §2.3

source_review.read_extent: Read the finite measurement definitions and probability formula in §2.3.
source_review.supports: Positive effects summing to identity specify outcome probabilities by the trace pairing.
source_review.limitations: The owned sharp-measurability and tomography proofs retain their exact finite-dimensional hypotheses.

sources.title: Richard Cleve, Quantum Information Processing, QIC 710 course notes, Fall 2023
sources.locator: Chapter 3 §§3.3.1–3.3.2 and 3.4–3.5, Theorems 3.1–3.2 and the Stinespring measurement discussion; PDF pp. 42–46.
sources.reading_extent: The complete relevant sections were inspected in the full 104-page course-note PDF; no claim is made that the remaining lecture notes were read for this batch.

contents.name: Kraus-to-Stinespring construction and outcome-register measurement, §§3.3.1–3.3.2

source_review.read_extent: Read the isometry construction, partial trace, and register measurement calculation.
source_review.supports: Embedding the Kraus labels into a finite ancilla yields an isometric dilation; measuring the register produces the Kraus outcome probability and residual map.
source_review.limitations: The authored theorem groups multiple Kraus labels under one outcome projection and proves the resulting partial-trace identity by matrix units.

contents.name: Measurements, channels, and coarse-graining a classical outcome, §3.4

source_review.read_extent: Read the complete finite-outcome channel/instrument discussion in §3.4.
source_review.supports: A classical outcome register and the remaining quantum state are distinct outputs of a measurement process.
source_review.limitations: The counterexample computes two exact qubit update maps and does not use a circuit diagram as proof.

contents.name: POVM outcomes do not determine residual states, §3.5

source_review.read_extent: Read the complete POVM discussion and its warning about residual state information in §3.5.
source_review.supports: Keeping only the outcome effects discards information needed to determine the post-measurement state update.
source_review.limitations: The exact Lüders and measure-and-prepare maps, effects, and input comparison are derived locally.

sources.title: Teiko Heinosaari, Daniel Reitzner, and Peter Stano, Notes on Joint Measurability of Quantum Observables
sources.locator: §1 introduction, §2 definitions (PDF pp. 2–3), and Appendix Proposition 8 (PDF p. 15).
sources.reading_extent: The complete relevant definition and sharp-observable proof passages were inspected in the full 17-page PDF; the paper’s unrelated later examples were not treated as suppliers.

contents.name: Finite observables and joint measurability, Definitions 1–2

source_review.read_extent: Read the finite-outcome marginal definition in §2.
source_review.supports: Joint measurability means one outcome family has the specified marginals.
source_review.limitations: The local theorem states its finite PVM and joint-POVM interfaces explicitly.

contents.name: A sharp observable in a joint measurement forces commutation, Appendix Proposition 8

source_review.read_extent: Read the complete proposition and proof in the Appendix.
source_review.supports: If one observable is sharp, any joint observable is supported in its projection ranges, which forces commutation and determines the joint effects.
source_review.limitations: The local proof gives the finite two-PVM specialization with an explicit positive-square-root support argument.

contents.name: General POVM commutativity is not equivalent to compatibility, §1

source_review.read_extent: Read the scope warning in the introduction.
source_review.supports: The sharp hypothesis is essential; general POVMs do not have the same simple commutation criterion.
source_review.limitations: The theorem’s Remarks preserve this scope boundary and do not classify general POVMs.

sources.title: Xhek Turkeshi and Markus Heinrich, Quantum Information Methods for Many-Body Physics, author-hosted course notes

sources.reading_extent: The complete §3.1 discussion of operator trace inner products, outcome probabilities, frame reconstruction, linear inversion, and informational completeness was inspected in the full 54-page notes; later classical-shadow sections were not claimed as relevant treatment.

contents.name: Operator trace inner product on matrices, equation (3.2)

source_review.read_extent: Read equation (3.2) and its adjacent definition of the trace inner product on L(H).
source_review.supports: The trace product is the natural finite-dimensional inner product on operator space.
source_review.limitations: The local lemma proves the real-valued restriction to Hermitian matrices and its positive definiteness directly.

contents.name: Informationally complete effects and frame reconstruction, §3.1 and Exercise 3.1

source_review.read_extent: Read the trace inner-product, frame-superoperator, dual-frame, and reconstruction discussion through Exercise 3.1.
source_review.supports: Spanning measurement effects permit linear recovery from outcome probabilities through dual operators.
source_review.limitations: The local proof handles redundant finite families by a Gram Moore–Penrose inverse and proves the required identity.

contents.name: Linear inversion tomography, equation (3.9)

source_review.read_extent: Read equation (3.9) and the surrounding derivation.
source_review.supports: The inverse frame operator defines a finite linear reconstruction procedure from exact probabilities.
source_review.limitations: The procedure uses the finite Gram pseudoinverse convention specified locally.

contents.name: The source’s measurement-effort estimate after equation (3.9)
contents.reason: The planned items do not state a trace-distance sample-complexity theorem; this source result requires different norms and a separate rank-sensitive analysis.

source_review.read_extent: Read the finite-copy scaling discussion following the linear-inversion formula.
source_review.supports: This result concerns trace-distance sample complexity and low-rank scaling.
source_review.limitations: The assigned theorem proves only an elementary uniform frequency-deviation bound and a Hilbert–Schmidt reconstruction error; no trace-distance complexity claim is in scope.
